classification.classification_note: The benchmark metadata phrases this issue as a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 8, but the saved Stage 01 runtime evidence is an AddressSanitizer `SEGV` on an unknown-address write in `TT_Get_MM_Var`. Source inspection shows the bug is a named-instance-count mismatch that under-allocates and under-initializes `mmvar`, then writes through a bogus `ns->coords` pointer.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42538854 (freetype2): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 8 found by fuzz target ftfuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42538854
bug_description.normalized: In `sfnt_init_face`, FreeType reads the font's `fvar` header and recognizes variation support, but the vulnerable code then unconditionally overwrites the parsed named-instance count whenever a `CFF ` table is present. For a font that also contains `glyf` and `gvar`, `sfnt_load_face` still marks the face as `FT_FACE_FLAG_MULTIPLE_MASTERS`, so `setIntermediateAxis(face)` calls `FT_Get_MM_Var`. `TT_Get_MM_Var` re-reads the true `fvar.instanceCount` from the font, but it allocates and initializes `mmvar` named-style storage from the reduced count cached in `face->style_flags`. When the later named-instance loop reaches a discarded instance, `ns->coords` is a bogus pointer and `*c = FT_GET_LONG()` performs the observed write-side crash at `src/truetype/ttgxvar.c:2144`.

source.code:
if ( face->goto_table( face, TTAG_fvar, stream, &fvar_len ) ||
     fvar_len < 20                                          ||
     FT_READ_ULONG( version )                               ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( offset )                               ||
     FT_STREAM_SKIP( 2 ) /* reserved */                     ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( num_axes )                             ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( axis_size )                            ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( num_instances )                        ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( instance_size ) )
source.description: First vulnerability-relevant project parser statement. It reads the attacker-controlled `fvar` header into local fields, including the font's named-instance count, and the valid-header path immediately below sets `face->variation_support |= TT_FACE_FLAG_VAR_FVAR`.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled sfnt/TTC bytes in the saved witness's `fvar` header and table directory. This statement materializes the `fvar` named-instance count before the later buggy `CFF `-table suppression overwrites the cached value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The loop bound that reaches the crashing write originates when `TT_Get_MM_Var` re-reads the attacker-controlled `fvar` header and materializes the actual `instanceCount` from the font.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The vulnerable code treats the mere presence of a `CFF ` table as grounds to discard the parsed `fvar` named-instance count, even when the same font also contains `glyf` and should still use the TrueType variation path. The fix changes this condition to zero the count only when `glyf` is absent and `CFF ` is present, and it moves the check after the default-instance synthesis block.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. After the named-instance loop advances past the initialized `mmvar->namedstyle[]` entries, `c` holds a bogus destination pointer read from non-`coords` bytes, and this assignment writes through it.
sink.note: The saved Stage 01 ASan trace reports `AddressSanitizer: SEGV`, `The signal is caused by a WRITE memory access`, and `SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: SEGV /src/freetype2/src/truetype/ttgxvar.c:2144:14 in TT_Get_MM_Var`.

parser_admitted.description: After `FT_New_Memory_Face` accepts the font and the harness is exercising the default instance (`instance_index == 0`), it enters the variable-font path by calling `setIntermediateAxis(face)`. The saved crash stack confirms this path reaches `TT_Get_MM_Var`.

coarse_trace.summary: FreeType reads the attacker's `fvar` header and marks variation support, but the vulnerable `CFF `-table check then discards the cached named-instance count before storing it in `face->style_flags`.
The same font still advertises `glyf`/`gvar`, so the loaded face is marked `FT_FACE_FLAG_MULTIPLE_MASTERS`; on the default-instance path the fuzzer therefore calls `FT_Get_MM_Var`.
`TT_Get_MM_Var` re-reads the true `fvar.instanceCount` from the font, but allocates and initializes `mmvar` named-style storage using the smaller count cached in `face->style_flags >> 16`.

The named-instance parser iterates the larger actual `fvar.instanceCount`, advances `ns` past the initialized `namedstyle` entries, loads a bogus `ns->coords` pointer, and crashes on `*c = FT_GET_LONG()`.

fine_trace.code:
if ( face->goto_table( face, TTAG_fvar, stream, &fvar_len ) ||
     fvar_len < 20                                          ||
     FT_READ_ULONG( version )                               ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( offset )                               ||
     FT_STREAM_SKIP( 2 ) /* reserved */                     ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( num_axes )                             ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( axis_size )                            ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( num_instances )                        ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( instance_size ) )
  { ... }
else
  face->variation_support |= TT_FACE_FLAG_VAR_FVAR;
fine_trace.note: Source. `sfnt_init_face` reads the attacker-controlled `fvar` header and materializes the font's named-instance count in local `num_instances`. On the valid-header path it also sets `face->variation_support |= TT_FACE_FLAG_VAR_FVAR`, preserving that the face is a variation font before any later instance-count rewriting.

Root cause. Any non-empty `CFF ` table forces `num_instances = 0`, even when the same font also contains `glyf` and should remain on the TrueType/GX variation path. The later default-instance synthesis can restore at most one entry, so the cached count no longer represents all actual `fvar` instances. The fix requires `glyf` to be absent before zeroing and moves this check after the synthesis block.

After the buggy suppression and any default-instance synthesis, the reduced retained instance count is cached in `face->root.style_flags >> 16`. `TT_Get_MM_Var` later reuses this cached count for allocation rather than the actual `fvar` header count.

Because step 1 already set `TT_FACE_FLAG_VAR_FVAR` and the same font directory still exposes `glyf` and `gvar`, face loading sets `FT_FACE_FLAG_MULTIPLE_MASTERS` anyway. The face now advertises Multiple Masters support while step 3's cached named-instance count understates the actual `fvar` instances.
On the default-instance path (`instance_index == 0`), the harness observes step 4's face flag and enters the variation/MM branch instead of returning early, calling `FT_Get_MM_Var` on this face.

`TT_Get_MM_Var` re-reads the attacker-controlled `fvar` header and materializes the actual `fvar_head.instanceCount` used by the named-instance parse loop. This count comes from the font, not from the reduced cache in step 3.

Allocation is sized from the reduced retained count cached in step 3, not from the actual `fvar_head.instanceCount` from step 6. `mmvar` therefore reserves named-style and coordinate space for only that smaller count.

Only the first `num_instances` `namedstyle[].coords` pointers are initialized to valid coordinate storage. Any additional actual `fvar` instances beyond that reduced count have no prepared `coords` pointer in `mmvar`.

The named-instance parse loop iterates the larger actual `fvar_head.instanceCount` from step 6 with no check that it fits the reduced allocation from steps 7-8. Once `i` reaches the first discarded instance, `ns` advances past the initialized `namedstyle` range.
For the first out-of-range `ns`, `ns->coords` is read from bytes that were never initialized as a valid `FT_Fixed*` coordinate array, so `c` becomes a bogus destination pointer.

The inner axis loop stores the next attacker-controlled coordinate through bogus `c`, causing the observed write-side crash. Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `AddressSanitizer: SEGV`, `The signal is caused by a WRITE memory access`, and points at `TT_Get_MM_Var /src/freetype2/src/truetype/ttgxvar.c:2144:14`.

format.name: sfnt/TTC variable font
format.contract: A font accepted by FreeType's SFNT loader whose table directory exposes a valid `fvar` variation header, `glyf`, and `gvar`, but also a non-empty `CFF ` table. The `CFF ` table must make the vulnerable `sfnt_init_face` cache fewer named instances in `face->style_flags >> 16` than `TT_Get_MM_Var` later re-reads from `fvar.instanceCount`; on the default-instance path (`instance_index == 0`) the harness then calls `setIntermediateAxis(face)`, `TT_Get_MM_Var` allocates and initializes `mmvar` for too few `namedstyle` entries, and the first discarded instance reaches `*c = FT_GET_LONG()` with a bogus `ns->coords` pointer.
